html:
The Statutes of Lithuania were three law codes of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania, issued in 1529, 1566 and 1588. They were among the most advanced legal codes of their time in Europe.

They gathered the law of the grand duchy in one book: the rights of nobles, courts, property and crimes. They were written in the Ruthenian chancery language, close to old Belarusian, since most of the grand duchy's people were Orthodox Ruthenians.

The third statute stayed in force even after Lithuania joined Poland in the Union of Lublin and was absorbed by the Russian Empire, until 1840. Lithuanians, Belarusians and Ukrainians all count it part of their heritage, a legacy of the Commonwealth. See Lithuania.
sum: The Statutes of Lithuania were three law codes of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania, issued in 1529, 1566 and 1588. They were among the most advanced legal codes of their time in Europe.
